docs.title: FortiGate Firewall – Block Social Media Websites (GUI)
FortiGate Firewall – Block Social Media Websites Using (GUI)
Overview
docs.text: FortiGate Web Filter allows network administrators to block access to specific websites like: www.youtube.com, www.facebook.com, www.instagram.com, domains, and URL paths.

docs.title: Configuration workflow
docs.text: Step 1         Create URL Filter Profile         Step 2         Apply Web Filter Profile         to Firewall Policy         Step 3         Test & Verify

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Web Filter Profile
docs.text:
1. Log in to the FortiGate GUI.

  2. Navigate to Security Profiles → Web Filter.

  3. Click Create New.

  4. Enter the profile name: Block-Social-Media.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Static URL Filter
docs.text:
Inside the new Web Filter profile:

  1. Find the Static URL Filter section.

  2. Enable URL Filter.

  3. Click Create New for each website.

  4. Add the following entries:

URL Type Action Status *youtube.com Wildcard Block Enable *facebook.com Wildcard Block Enable *instagram.com Wildcard Block Enable Purpose: Adds the social media websites to the URL block list.

Use the following example configuration: (Screenshot):

docs.title: Step 3: Apply the Profile to the Firewall Policy
docs.text:
A URL filter will not protect users unless the applicable traffic passes through a firewall policy with the Web Filter profile enabled.

  1. Go to Policy & Objects → Firewall Policy.

  2. Identify the policy that allows users to access the internet.

  3. Edit that policy.

  4. Enable Security Profiles or UTM Inspection, depending on the FortiOS version.

  5. Enable Web Filter.

  6. Select the profile Block-Social-Media.

  7. Enable SSL/SSH inspection as appropriate for your network.

  8. Save the policy.

Important: Edit the correct internet access policy. Do not change unrelated policies.

Use the following example configuration: (Screenshot):

docs.title: Step 4: Test the Configuration
docs.text:
1. Connect a client computer to the network.

  2. Open YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram.

  3. Confirm that the websites are blocked.

  4. If YouTube videos still play, check HTTPS inspection, QUIC/HTTP/3 traffic, and whether the correct firewall policy is being used.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text:
YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram should be blocked for users whose internet traffic passes through the configured firewall policy. Websites not matched by a blocking rule should remain accessible.

Note: GUI menu names can differ between FortiOS versions. Configuration must be tested on a client device to confirm that blocking is working.

docs.title: Check Web Filter logs
docs.text:
If the website is still accessible, check the logs:

  1. Navigate to Log & Report → Security Events.

  2. Open the Web Filter events.

  3. Filter for the client's source IP address or the destination hostname.

  4. Review the action, matched URL, profile, and policy ID.

  5. Look for an entry with an action such as blocked and a message indicating that the URL matched the local URL filter.

Use the following example configuration: (Screenshot):

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: FortiGate firewalls also allow administrators to block Web Filter feature and firewall policies using graphical user interface (GUI) as well as Command Line Interface (CLI).

docs.title: Step 1: Create the URL Filter Table
docs.text:
1. Log in to the FortiGate firewall using SSH, a console connection, or the CLI Console available in the web interface.

  2. First, create a URL filter table and add a rule to block social media sites.

config webfilter urlfilter
    edit 1
        set name "Social-Media-URLs"
        config entries
            edit 1
                set url "*youtube.com"
                set type wildcard
                set action block
            next
            edit 2
                set url "*facebook.com"
                set type wildcard
                set action block
            next
            edit 3
                set url "*instagram.com"
                set type wildcard
                set action block
            next
        end
    next
end

Purpose: Creates a URL Filter table containing the websites to be blocked.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure the Web Filter Profile
docs.text:
config webfilter profile
    edit "Block-Social-Media"
        config web
            set urlfilter-table 1
        end
    next
end

Purpose: Links URL Filter table ID 1 to the Block-Social-Media profile.

docs.title: Step 3: Apply the Profile to the Firewall Policy
docs.text:
First, identify the firewall policy used for internet access:

show firewall policy

Use the actual policy ID in the following commands. The example below uses policy ID 1.

config firewall policy
    edit 1
        set utm-status enable
        set webfilter-profile "Block-Social-Media"
    next
end

Purpose: Enables security inspection and applies the custom Web Filter profile to the selected firewall policy.

Important: Modify the correct internet access policy to avoid affecting other network traffic.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Configuration
docs.text:
Check the URL Filter table

show webfilter urlfilter

Check the Web Filter profile

show webfilter profile "Block-Social-Media"

Check the firewall policy

show firewall policy

Confirm that the correct policy has the following settings

set utm-status enable
set webfilter-profile "Block-Social-Media"

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text:
• YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram should be blocked for users whose traffic passes through the configured firewall policy.

  • The custom Web Filter profile should be applied to the correct policy.

  • Test the websites from a client computer to confirm that blocking works.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If YouTube videos still play after applying the configuration, check HTTPS inspection, QUIC/HTTP/3 traffic, and whether the traffic is actually passing through the configured policy.

Note: Configuration alone does not guarantee successful blocking. Always test and verify the result on the client device.

docs.title: Important Consideration:
docs.text:
1. Correct Policy ID: Verify that you are modifying the correct LAN-to-WAN firewall policy handling the client's traffic.

  2. Profile Association: Ensure the Static URL Filter list is linked to the intended Web Filter profile and that the profile is applied to the relevant firewall policies.

  3. Wildcard Matching: Configure URL patterns carefully, such as *facebook.com, because matching behavior may vary with the pattern and FortiOS version.

  4. HTTPS Inspection: URL filtering capabilities depend on the SSL inspection profile and the visibility available for encrypted traffic.

  5. Additional Domains: Applications may use additional domains, content delivery networks (CDNs), and alternate endpoints. Blocking one domain may not block the entire application.

  6. QUIC and HTTP/3: These protocols can affect filtering behavior. Review QUIC handling if blocking is incomplete.

  7. Existing Configuration: Review existing firewall and security profiles before making changes to avoid overwriting required settings.

  8. FortiOS Compatibility: Confirm command syntax and supported features for your FortiGate FortiOS version.

  9. Production Deployment: Test changes in a controlled environment before applying them to production networks.

Official Reference: Fortinet's FortiOS 7.4.8 Administration Guide. Your interface may differ slightly. Reference Source: Fortinet — Static URL Filter and verification

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: Blocking a website on FortiGate using CLI involves three main tasks: configuring a Static URL Filter, associating it with a Web Filter profile, and applying that profile to the appropriate firewall policy.

docs.title: SOP-001: PROPERTY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (PMS) OPERATIONS & SUPPORT
docs.text: Department: Information Technology Document ID: HIT-SOP-001 Version: 1.0 Document Type: Standard Operating Procedure Applicability: Hotel IT Departments Review Frequency: Annually or whenever significant system changes occur Prepared By: IT Department Approved By: Authorized Hotel Management

docs.title: 1. PURPOSE
docs.text:
The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure is to establish a standardized process for the operation, monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, security and technical support of the Property Management System (PMS) used in hotel operations.

The PMS is a critical hotel application responsible for supporting various operational activities, including reservations, guest check-in and check-out, room management, billing, cashiering, guest profiles and operational reporting.

This SOP ensures that the PMS remains available, secure, properly configured and accessible to authorized users, minimizing operational interruptions and protecting hotel and guest information.

docs.title: 2. SCOPE
docs.text:
This SOP applies to all PMS-related IT operations and technical support activities, including:

  • PMS application availability and monitoring.

  • PMS user account creation and management.

  • User access and permission control.

  • Login and application troubleshooting.

  • PMS workstation and terminal support.

  • PMS-related network connectivity.

  • Integration and interface monitoring.

  • Database and application backup coordination.

  • PMS updates and maintenance coordination.

  • Incident reporting and escalation.

  • PMS downtime and recovery support.

  • Vendor coordination and technical documentation.

This SOP applies whether the PMS is cloud-hosted, locally hosted, server-based or provided through a managed service.

docs.title: 3.1 IT Manager
docs.text:
The IT Manager is responsible for:

  • Overall PMS technical administration and support oversight.

  • Ensuring system availability and operational reliability.

  • Coordinating with PMS vendors and service providers.

  • Reviewing user access and permissions periodically.

  • Monitoring recurring technical issues.

  • Approving or coordinating technical changes according to hotel authorization procedures.

  • Ensuring backup and recovery arrangements are maintained.

  • Maintaining PMS-related technical documentation.

  • Reporting critical system issues to hotel management.

docs.title: 3.2 IT Executive / IT Support Engineer
docs.text:
Responsibilities include:

  • Providing first-level PMS technical support.

  • Troubleshooting login and connectivity problems.

  • Checking PMS workstation and peripheral connectivity.

  • Logging and tracking reported incidents.

  • Performing authorized user administration.

  • Monitoring system availability.

  • Coordinating with vendors for unresolved issues.

  • Maintaining technical support records.

  • Following escalation procedures.

docs.title: 3.3 Front Office Department
docs.text:
Responsibilities include:

  • Reporting PMS operational problems to IT.

  • Ensuring that employees use their assigned accounts.

  • Reporting incorrect access or suspicious account activity.

  • Following approved operational procedures during PMS downtime.

  • Verifying operational transactions after system recovery.

  • Coordinating with IT for user access requirements.

docs.title: 3.4 Authorized PMS Vendor / Service Provider
docs.text:
Responsibilities may include:

  • Application-level technical support.

  • Advanced troubleshooting.

  • Software updates and bug fixes.

  • Database-level technical support.

  • Integration troubleshooting.

  • Backup and recovery assistance, where contracted.

  • Escalated incident resolution.

docs.title: 3.5 Department Heads / Authorized Approvers
docs.text:
Responsibilities include:

  • Approving employee access requests.

  • Confirming required user roles and permissions.

  • Authorizing changes affecting departmental operations.

  • Reviewing access requirements when employees transfer or leave.

docs.title: 4.1 New User Account Creation
docs.text:
The following procedure must be followed when creating a new PMS user account:

  1. Receive a formal user access request from the concerned department head or authorized manager.

  2. Verify the employee's identity and department.

  3. Confirm the required PMS role and access permissions.

  4. Obtain the necessary approval before creating the account.

  5. Create an individual user account using the employee's authorized identification.

  6. Assign only the permissions required for the employee's job responsibilities.

  7. Configure password and authentication requirements according to the PMS security capabilities and hotel policy.

  8. Ensure that default or temporary passwords are changed before normal use.

  9. Inform the employee about account confidentiality and acceptable usage.

  10. Record the account creation details in the PMS User Access Register.

Important: Shared user accounts must not be used for routine individual employee activities. Each employee should have a uniquely identifiable account wherever the PMS supports it.

docs.title: 4.2 User Access Modification
docs.text:
When an employee changes department, designation or job responsibilities:

  1. Receive an approved access modification request.

  2. Review the employee's existing permissions.

  3. Confirm the new role with the concerned department head.

  4. Remove unnecessary permissions.

  5. Assign the newly approved permissions.

  6. Verify that the updated access works correctly.

  7. Update the user access register.

docs.title: 4.3 User Account Deactivation
docs.text:
When an employee resigns, is terminated or no longer requires PMS access:

  1. Receive an authorized employee separation or access removal notification.

  2. Verify the employee's identity and account details.

  3. Disable or deactivate the PMS account according to the approved timeline.

  4. Revoke associated sessions, tokens or remote access where applicable.

  5. Coordinate removal of related access to connected systems if required.

  6. Update the PMS User Access Register.

  7. Retain relevant records according to hotel policy.

For urgent terminations or suspected unauthorized access, account deactivation must be coordinated immediately with the authorized management team.

docs.title: 5. DAILY PMS SYSTEM MONITORING
docs.text: The IT team should perform the following checks according to the hotel's operational schedule.

docs.title: 5.1 Application Availability
docs.text:
• Verify that the PMS application is accessible.

  • Check application login functionality.

  • Confirm that authorized users can access their respective modules.

  • Identify unexpected application errors or service interruptions.

  • Verify application connectivity for critical operational workstations.

docs.title: 5.2 Workstation Connectivity
docs.text:
• Check PMS-connected workstations.

  • Verify LAN or Wi-Fi connectivity, as applicable.

  • Check system date and time synchronization.

  • Verify printer and peripheral connectivity where integrated with PMS.

  • Identify abnormal system performance or application freezing.

docs.title: 5.3 Interface and Integration Monitoring
docs.text:
Where integrations are implemented, check the status of relevant interfaces, such as:

  • POS integration.

  • Payment gateway integration.

  • Channel manager and booking engine integration.

  • Key card / electronic door lock integration.

  • Telephone / EPABX integration.

  • Guest Wi-Fi integration.

  • Accounting and financial system integration.

  • Other approved third-party applications.

Check for failed transactions, synchronization delays, interface errors or communication failures.

Note: Operational transaction verification belongs to the authorized business department. IT is responsible for technical interface monitoring and troubleshooting.

docs.title: 5.4 Database and Server Health
docs.text:
For locally hosted or IT-managed environments:

  • Check relevant PMS application services.

  • Monitor database availability.

  • Review available storage capacity.

  • Check server resource utilization.

  • Review critical application and database error logs.

  • Verify backup job completion status.

For cloud-hosted PMS environments:

  • Check service availability through the vendor's official status portal, where available.

  • Review service notifications and maintenance announcements.

  • Report suspected cloud service outages to the provider.

  • Maintain records of service interruptions.

docs.title: 6. PMS TROUBLESHOOTING PROCEDURE
docs.text: When a PMS-related complaint is received, IT personnel must follow a structured troubleshooting process.

docs.title: Step 1: Register the Complaint
docs.text:
Record the following information:

  • Date and time of complaint.

  • Name and department of the reporting employee.

  • Workstation or terminal identification.

  • PMS module affected.

  • Description of the issue.

  • Error message or screenshot, where appropriate and safe.

  • Number of affected users.

  • Operational impact.

docs.title: Step 2: Identify the Problem Category
docs.text:
Classify the problem into one of the following categories:

  • User login issue.

  • Password or account issue.

  • Application access issue.

  • Network connectivity issue.

  • Workstation performance issue.

  • Printer or peripheral issue.

  • PMS application error.

  • Database connectivity issue.

  • Integration or interface failure.

  • Vendor-side service interruption.

docs.title: Step 3: Perform Initial Checks
docs.text:
1. Verify network connectivity.

  2. Check whether the issue affects one user or multiple users.

  3. Verify application availability.

  4. Check workstation health.

  5. Confirm the affected user's access permissions.

  6. Review relevant application or system error messages.

  7. Check vendor service notifications if the PMS is cloud-hosted.

docs.title: Step 4: Resolve or Escalate
docs.text:
• Resolve issues within the IT team's authorized technical capabilities.

  • Do not make unauthorized application or database changes.

  • Escalate application-level issues to the PMS vendor when required.

  • Inform the IT Manager about critical operational interruptions.

  • Coordinate with the affected department until normal operations are restored.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Resolution
docs.text:
• Confirm that the affected user can access the system.

  • Verify that the reported functionality is working.

  • Obtain confirmation from the concerned department.

  • Update the complaint or incident record.

  • Document the root cause and corrective action where identified.

docs.title: 7. PMS CHANGE AND UPDATE MANAGEMENT
docs.text:
Any change affecting PMS configuration, application functionality, integrations or infrastructure must follow an approved change management process.

Examples include:

  • PMS software upgrades.

  • Application patches.

  • Configuration modifications.

  • User role changes.

  • Interface configuration changes.

  • Database changes.

  • Server migrations.

  • Network configuration changes affecting PMS connectivity.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Identify the requirement for change.

  2. Record the proposed change and its business justification.

  3. Assess operational impact and associated risks.

  4. Obtain authorization from the appropriate management representative.

  5. Coordinate with the PMS vendor where required.

  6. Schedule the change during an approved maintenance window.

  7. Confirm that suitable backups or recovery arrangements are available.

  8. Inform affected departments before implementation.

  9. Perform the approved change.

  10. Test critical PMS functions after implementation.

  11. Obtain confirmation from the concerned operational department.

  12. Document the change and its outcome.

Important: Changes involving live PMS databases, financial records or guest information must only be performed by authorized personnel following approved vendor and hotel procedures.

docs.title: 8. PMS BACKUP AND DATA RECOVERY COORDINATION
docs.text:
PMS data is critical to hotel operations and business continuity.

The IT Manager must ensure that appropriate backup and recovery arrangements exist.

docs.title: 8.1 Backup Requirements
docs.text:
• Identify whether PMS data is stored locally, remotely or in the cloud.

  • Confirm the party responsible for performing backups.

  • Obtain documented information about backup frequency and retention.

  • Verify backup job status wherever IT has access.

  • Ensure backup storage is protected against unauthorized access.

  • Confirm that recovery procedures are documented.

  • Coordinate periodic restoration testing with the responsible provider.

docs.title: 8.2 Backup Failure
docs.text:
If a backup failure is identified:

  1. Record the failure date and time.

  2. Identify the affected backup job or system.

  3. Notify the IT Manager.

  4. Contact the responsible technical team or PMS vendor.

  5. Confirm whether a successful alternative recovery point exists.

  6. Track the issue until resolved.

  7. Record corrective action and confirmation of successful backup completion.

docs.title: 8.3 Data Restoration
docs.text:
Data restoration must be performed only after proper authorization and impact assessment.

The following steps must be followed:

  1. Identify the reason for restoration.

  2. Determine the required recovery point.

  3. Obtain management authorization.

  4. Coordinate with the PMS vendor or authorized database administrator.

  5. Confirm the availability and integrity of the backup.

  6. Perform restoration according to the approved recovery procedure.

  7. Verify system functionality and data consistency.

  8. Obtain confirmation from the relevant operational department.

  9. Record the restoration activity.

docs.title: 9. PMS DOWNTIME MANAGEMENT
docs.text:
PMS downtime can directly affect reservations, guest check-in, check-out, room allocation and billing activities.

The IT department must follow a controlled downtime management process.

docs.title: 9.1 Initial Response
docs.text:
1. Identify whether the outage affects one workstation, multiple users or the entire hotel.

  2. Determine whether the issue is related to network infrastructure, application services, database services or the PMS provider.

  3. Record the start time of the interruption.

  4. Inform the IT Manager.

  5. Notify affected departments through the approved communication channel.

  6. Contact the PMS vendor if the issue is application-related or outside IT's control.

docs.title: 9.2 Operational Coordination
docs.text:
During downtime:

  • Inform the Front Office Manager and other affected department heads.

  • Ensure that the hotel follows its approved PMS downtime procedure.

  • Coordinate with authorized operational personnel for manual records where required.

  • Ensure that sensitive guest and financial information is protected.

  • Avoid duplicate or unauthorized transactions during manual operations.

docs.title: 9.3 System Restoration
docs.text:
After PMS services are restored:

  1. Confirm system availability.

  2. Test login functionality.

  3. Verify critical modules.

  4. Check relevant interfaces and integrations.

  5. Coordinate with Front Office and other departments for pending transaction reconciliation.

  6. Confirm that authorized personnel have completed necessary manual data updates.

  7. Record the restoration time.

  8. Close the incident after obtaining appropriate confirmation.

Note: IT personnel must not independently create, modify or reconcile guest reservations, room charges or financial transactions unless specifically authorized and trained to do so.

docs.title: 10. PMS SECURITY MANAGEMENT
docs.text:
The IT department must ensure that PMS access and technical infrastructure follow the hotel's information security requirements.

Minimum security practices include:

  • Individual user accounts.

  • Role-based access control.

  • Strong password requirements.

  • Multi-factor authentication wherever supported.

  • Periodic access reviews.

  • Immediate deactivation of unauthorized or unnecessary accounts.

  • Restricted administrative privileges.

  • Secure remote vendor access.

  • Protection of guest and financial information.

  • Monitoring of relevant security logs.

  • Timely security updates in coordination with the vendor.

  • Prohibition of unauthorized software installation.

Administrative accounts must be restricted to authorized personnel.

Vendor remote access must be approved, time-limited where possible, monitored and disabled after the support requirement is completed.

docs.title: 11. PMS VENDOR COORDINATION
docs.text:
The IT department must maintain proper coordination with the PMS service provider.

The following information should be maintained:

  • Vendor name and contact details.

  • Support email address and telephone number.

  • Customer or property identification.

  • Contract and AMC details, where applicable.

  • Support coverage and service hours.

  • Escalation contacts.

  • System hosting and infrastructure details.

  • Integration information.

  • Current software version.

  • Known issues and pending tickets.

For every vendor complaint:

  1. Register the issue internally.

  2. Create a vendor support ticket.

  3. Record the vendor ticket reference.

  4. Provide relevant technical details.

  5. Track progress.

  6. Escalate unresolved critical issues.

  7. Verify the resolution.

  8. Maintain closure records.

docs.title: 12. PMS DOCUMENTATION AND RECORD MANAGEMENT
docs.text:
The IT department must maintain the following records:

Record Purpose PMS User Access Register User account and permission tracking PMS Incident Register Complaint and issue tracking PMS Downtime Register Outage and recovery records PMS Vendor Support Register Vendor complaint tracking PMS Change Log Configuration and software change history PMS Backup Verification Log Backup monitoring PMS Maintenance Log Preventive and corrective maintenance PMS Integration Register Connected systems and interface details

All records must be maintained in an approved, access-controlled location according to hotel retention requirements.

Passwords, authentication secrets and sensitive guest information must never be stored in ordinary registers or unsecured documents.

docs.title: 13. PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE
docs.text:
The IT team must follow a preventive maintenance schedule based on system architecture, vendor recommendations and operational requirements.

Suggested activities:

Daily

  • Check PMS availability.

  • Review reported technical issues.

  • Check critical integration status.

  • Review backup status where accessible.

Weekly

  • Review recurring complaints.

  • Check unresolved vendor tickets.

  • Review system and application error logs where accessible.

  • Check server or cloud service alerts.

Monthly

  • Review user access changes.

  • Review system performance.

  • Verify backup monitoring records.

  • Review pending application updates.

  • Review vendor support issues.

Quarterly

  • Conduct a detailed access review with department heads.

  • Review vendor escalation details.

  • Verify documented recovery procedures.

  • Review recurring incidents and improvement opportunities.

Actual frequency may be adjusted according to vendor recommendations, system architecture and hotel operational requirements.

docs.title: 14. INCIDENT ESCALATION MATRIX
docs.text:
The following is a suggested escalation framework. Actual response targets should be established through hotel policy and vendor support agreements.

Priority Example Escalation Critical Complete PMS outage affecting hotel operations IT Manager, PMS Vendor, Hotel Management High Multiple users or critical PMS modules unavailable IT Manager, PMS Vendor Medium Individual module or workstation issue IT Executive, IT Manager Low Minor user assistance or non-critical configuration request IT Support Team

For security incidents involving suspected unauthorized access, data exposure or compromised accounts, the IT Manager and designated information security or management representatives must be notified immediately.

docs.title: 15. PMS PERFORMANCE MONITORING
docs.text:
The IT Manager should periodically review the following operational indicators:

  • PMS availability and downtime.

  • Number of PMS-related incidents.

  • Average incident resolution time.

  • Number of recurring technical complaints.

  • Pending vendor support tickets.

  • Backup success rate, where measurable.

  • User access review completion.

  • Critical interface failure frequency.

  • Preventive maintenance completion.

These indicators should be reviewed to identify operational weaknesses and opportunities for improvement.

docs.title: Daily PMS Checklist
docs.text:
• PMS application availability verified.

  • Login functionality checked.

  • Critical PMS modules accessible.

  • PMS workstation connectivity checked.

  • Critical integrations reviewed.

  • Backup status checked where applicable.

  • Reported PMS complaints reviewed.

  • Critical vendor alerts reviewed.

  • Pending critical incidents escalated.

  • Daily checks recorded.

docs.title: Monthly PMS Checklist
docs.text:
• User access review completed.

  • Unauthorized or inactive accounts reviewed.

  • Pending software updates reviewed.

  • Vendor support tickets reviewed.

  • Backup monitoring records verified.

  • Recovery arrangements reviewed.

  • PMS documentation updated.

  • Recurring issues analyzed.

  • Monthly PMS performance reviewed.

docs.title: 17. HOTEL-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
docs.text:
This SOP provides a common operational framework. Certain activities may differ depending on the PMS platform and hotel infrastructure.

Examples:

  • Cloud PMS platforms may not provide direct server or database administration access to hotel IT personnel.

  • On-premises PMS platforms may require local server, database and application service monitoring.

  • Some PMS platforms provide integrated user management, while others require vendor assistance.

  • Backup responsibilities may belong to the hotel, PMS vendor or cloud service provider.

  • Certain interfaces may be managed by third-party vendors.

  • Administrative permissions and available monitoring features may vary by software platform.

The IT Manager must document these differences in the hotel's PMS technical documentation without compromising the minimum controls established by this SOP.

docs.title: 18. COMPLIANCE AND EXCEPTIONS
docs.text:
All IT personnel involved in PMS support must follow this SOP and the applicable hotel information security policies.

Any exception must be documented, justified and approved by the appropriate management authority.

Unauthorized system access, unapproved configuration changes, sharing of credentials and disclosure of guest information are strictly prohibited.

Applicable privacy, cybersecurity, contractual and regulatory requirements must also be followed.

docs.title: 19. REVIEW AND REVISION HISTORY
docs.text:
This SOP must be reviewed annually or whenever significant changes occur in PMS technology, hotel operations, security requirements or applicable regulations.

Version Date Description Prepared By 1.0 Initial Issue First release IT Department

Document End

Disclaimer: This is a general hotel IT operations template. Each hotel should validate its implementation against its PMS vendor documentation, contractual responsibilities, internal policies and applicable legal requirements.

docs.title: POS OPERATIONS & SUPPORT
docs.text: Department: Information Technology (IT) SOP Category: Hotel Application Systems SOP Number: SOP-002 Document Type: Standard Operating Procedure Applicable To: Hotels, Resorts, Restaurants, Bars, Banquet Operations and Other Food & Beverage Outlets Process Owner: IT Department Review Frequency: Annually or whenever a major operational or system change occurs Version: 1.0 Effective Date: As approved by hotel management

docs.title: 1. PURPOSE
docs.text:
The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure is to establish a consistent process for the operation, monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, and support of the hotel's Point of Sale (POS) system.

The POS system is an essential operational application used by Food & Beverage outlets to record orders, process payments, manage billing, and transfer charges to guest accounts through integration with the Property Management System (PMS).

This SOP ensures:

  • Reliable availability of POS services.

  • Accurate order entry and billing operations.

  • Proper integration between POS and PMS.

  • Controlled user access and permissions.

  • Timely resolution of technical issues.

  • Secure handling of transaction and guest information.

  • Proper coordination between IT, Food & Beverage, Finance, and system vendors.

  • Consistent documentation of system activities and incidents.

docs.title: 2. SCOPE
docs.text:
This SOP applies to all POS systems and related equipment used within the hotel.

It covers:

  • Restaurant POS terminals.

  • Bar and lounge POS terminals.

  • Room service POS terminals.

  • Banquet and event POS terminals.

  • Poolside and outdoor POS terminals.

  • Kitchen order display systems (KDS).

  • POS printers and kitchen printers.

  • Handheld POS devices and tablets.

  • POS software and databases.

  • POS application servers or cloud services.

  • POS-to-PMS integration.

  • POS network connectivity.

  • Payment terminal connectivity, where applicable.

  • POS user accounts and access permissions.

  • POS backups, updates, and vendor support.

This SOP applies whether the POS system is cloud-based, locally hosted, centrally hosted, or integrated with other hotel applications.

docs.title: 3.1 IT Manager / IT Head
docs.text:
• Overall ownership of POS system technical operations.

  • Ensure POS availability and support arrangements.

  • Approve technical changes and access requests according to hotel policy.

  • Coordinate with vendors for major technical issues.

  • Monitor recurring incidents and system performance.

  • Ensure appropriate backup and recovery arrangements.

  • Review system security and access controls.

docs.title: 3.2 IT Executive / IT Support Engineer
docs.text:
• Monitor POS system availability.

  • Provide first-level technical support.

  • Troubleshoot POS terminals, printers, network connectivity, and application issues.

  • Coordinate with the POS vendor for unresolved problems.

  • Maintain technical documentation and incident records.

  • Verify system functionality after maintenance or changes.

  • Assist authorized departments with approved configuration activities.

docs.title: 3.3 Food & Beverage Manager
docs.text:
• Ensure operational compliance with POS procedures.

  • Approve or recommend POS user access according to departmental authority.

  • Ensure staff receive appropriate system training.

  • Report operational issues to IT.

  • Validate outlet-level functionality and billing workflows.

docs.title: 3.4 Restaurant / Outlet Manager
docs.text:
• Monitor POS operations within the assigned outlet.

  • Ensure correct order entry and billing practices.

  • Report POS issues promptly.

  • Verify printer, order routing, and billing functionality.

  • Ensure staff use individual authorized accounts.

docs.title: 3.5 Finance / Accounts Department
docs.text:
• Monitor POS transaction and revenue reconciliation.

  • Verify billing and payment-related discrepancies.

  • Coordinate with IT regarding financial reporting or transaction integration issues.

  • Approve financial configuration changes where required.

docs.title: 3.6 POS System Vendor
docs.text:
• Provide application-level technical support.

  • Assist with software errors and advanced troubleshooting.

  • Support approved upgrades and configuration changes.

  • Assist with database and application recovery.

  • Provide technical documentation and escalation support.

docs.title: 4.1 New User Creation
docs.text:
1. Receive a formal POS access request from the authorized department head or manager.

  2. Verify the employee's identity and department.

  3. Confirm the required outlet and job role.

  4. Obtain approval from the designated authority.

  5. Create the user account using the approved POS administration process.

  6. Assign only the permissions necessary for the employee's job responsibilities.

  7. Configure an individual user ID and secure authentication method.

  8. Avoid sharing administrator or employee credentials.

  9. Ask the department to verify the account's functionality.

  10. Record the account creation in the POS access register.

docs.title: 4.2 User Role and Permission Modification
docs.text:
1. Receive an approved request for the required modification.

  2. Verify the employee's current role and revised responsibilities.

  3. Review the requested permissions.

  4. Obtain approval from the authorized department head.

  5. Modify the required permissions.

  6. Verify that unrelated permissions have not been granted.

  7. Test the updated access with the relevant department.

  8. Update the access register.

docs.title: 4.3 User Deactivation
docs.text:
1. Receive an employee separation, transfer, or access-removal notification.

  2. Verify the employee details and effective date.

  3. Obtain confirmation from HR or the authorized department.

  4. Disable or deactivate the POS account within the required timeframe.

  5. Revoke any associated privileged access.

  6. Preserve transaction audit records according to hotel retention policy.

  7. Update the POS access register.

Important: Individual POS accounts must not be shared between employees. Privileged accounts must be restricted to authorized personnel.

docs.title: 5. DAILY POS SYSTEM MONITORING
docs.text: The IT team should perform daily checks to confirm that POS services are operational.

docs.title: 5.1 Application Availability
docs.text:
1. Verify that the POS application is accessible.

  2. Confirm that the application server or cloud service is available.

  3. Check for error messages or unexpected application behaviour.

  4. Confirm that authorized users can log in.

  5. Review available system alerts and logs.

docs.title: 5.2 POS Terminal Verification
docs.text:
1. Check the operational status of active POS terminals.

  2. Confirm that each terminal can connect to the POS application.

  3. Verify that the correct outlet and terminal configuration is displayed.

  4. Check date and time synchronization.

  5. Confirm that no unauthorized software or configuration changes are present.

docs.title: 5.3 Printer Verification
docs.text:
1. Check receipt printers and kitchen printers.

  2. Confirm paper availability.

  3. Verify printer connectivity.

  4. Print a test receipt where operationally appropriate.

  5. Confirm that kitchen orders are reaching the correct printer or display system.

  6. Report recurring printer issues to the IT team.

docs.title: 5.4 PMS Integration Verification
docs.text:
Where POS is integrated with the hotel PMS:

  1. Confirm that the POS can communicate with the PMS.

  2. Verify that authorized room-charge transactions can be processed.

  3. Confirm that room and guest information is being retrieved correctly.

  4. Review any failed or pending transaction messages.

  5. Coordinate with Front Office and Finance if a transaction discrepancy is identified.

docs.title: 5.5 Network Connectivity
docs.text:
1. Verify network connectivity at POS locations.

  2. Check wired or wireless connections, depending on the installation.

  3. Confirm that required application services are reachable.

  4. Report network interruptions to the network support team.

  5. Avoid making unauthorized network configuration changes.

docs.title: 6. POS ORDER AND BILLING SUPPORT
docs.text: The IT team is responsible for technical support of POS order and billing functionality. Operational decisions regarding order entry, discounts, voids, and financial adjustments remain with authorized Food & Beverage and Finance personnel.

docs.title: 6.1 Order Entry Issues
docs.text:
If a user reports that orders cannot be entered:

  1. Confirm whether the issue affects one terminal or multiple terminals.

  2. Verify POS application availability.

  3. Check terminal connectivity.

  4. Confirm that the user account is active.

  5. Review relevant application error messages.

  6. Restart the application only when appropriate and after considering active transactions.

  7. Escalate unresolved application errors to the POS vendor.

  8. Ask the outlet to verify order entry after resolution.

docs.title: 6.2 Billing Issues
docs.text:
If a billing issue is reported:

  1. Obtain the transaction reference, outlet, terminal, and approximate transaction time.

  2. Identify the reported error.

  3. Check application connectivity and relevant transaction status.

  4. Review available logs or transaction records.

  5. Coordinate with Finance and the outlet manager to verify the transaction.

  6. Avoid editing, deleting, or recreating financial transactions without proper authorization.

  7. Escalate application-level billing errors to the vendor.

  8. Document the resolution.

docs.title: 6.3 Discount, Void, and Refund Issues
docs.text:
1. Verify whether the issue is related to system permissions or application functionality.

  2. Confirm that the employee has the appropriate authorization.

  3. Refer financial approval requirements to the designated departmental authority.

  4. Do not independently approve or process financial adjustments as an IT activity.

  5. Record technical changes and support actions.

  6. Escalate suspicious or unauthorized activity through the hotel's established control process.

docs.title: 7. POS PRINTER AND KITCHEN DISPLAY SYSTEM SUPPORT
7.1 Receipt Printer Troubleshooting
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the printer is powered on.

  2. Check paper roll availability and correct installation.

  3. Check printer cable or network connectivity.

  4. Verify that the correct printer is selected in the POS configuration.

  5. Print a test receipt.

  6. Check for paper jams or hardware warnings.

  7. Restart the printer if safe and appropriate.

  8. Replace faulty consumables or arrange hardware repair.

  9. Record repeated failures.

docs.title: 7.2 Kitchen Printer Troubleshooting
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the kitchen printer is powered on.

  2. Verify network or cable connectivity.

  3. Check the printer queue, where available.

  4. Confirm that the relevant outlet and order category are correctly mapped.

  5. Verify whether orders are reaching other kitchen printers.

  6. Test order routing with the authorized outlet representative.

  7. Escalate application configuration issues to the POS vendor.

docs.title: 7.3 Kitchen Display System (KDS)
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the display is powered on.

  2. Verify network connectivity.

  3. Check application login and display status.

  4. Confirm that new orders are appearing.

  5. Verify order routing and status updates.

  6. Escalate application or integration problems to the vendor.

docs.title: 8. POS AND PMS INTEGRATION MANAGEMENT
docs.text: Where POS and PMS are integrated, IT must ensure that the communication between the systems remains operational.

docs.title: 8.1 Integration Monitoring
docs.text:
1. Monitor the availability of the POS-PMS interface.

  2. Check for failed, delayed, or pending transactions.

  3. Verify that room-charge posting functionality is available.

  4. Review integration error logs where accessible.

  5. Coordinate with Front Office and Finance for transaction verification.

docs.title: 8.2 Room Charge Posting Issues
docs.text:
If room charges cannot be posted:

  1. Confirm that the guest room information is available in the POS.

  2. Verify whether the issue affects one guest or multiple guests.

  3. Check POS and PMS connectivity.

  4. Confirm the status of the integration service.

  5. Coordinate with Front Office to verify the guest account and posting eligibility.

  6. Do not bypass financial or guest verification controls.

  7. Escalate unresolved interface problems to the vendor.

  8. Verify the transaction status after recovery.

docs.title: 8.3 Integration Failure
docs.text:
If the interface stops working:

  1. Identify the time when the failure started.

  2. Determine which outlets and transactions are affected.

  3. Notify the IT Manager, Front Office, F&B, and Finance as appropriate.

  4. Contact the POS or PMS vendor according to the support arrangement.

  5. Follow the approved downtime procedure.

  6. Ensure that pending transactions are reconciled after service restoration.

docs.title: 9. POS DOWNTIME MANAGEMENT
docs.text: POS downtime may occur due to application failure, network interruption, server problems, power failure, database errors, or cloud service outages.

docs.title: 9.1 Initial Response
docs.text:
1. Receive the downtime complaint.

  2. Record the time and affected outlet or terminals.

  3. Determine whether the issue is local or system-wide.

  4. Check power, network connectivity, application availability, and relevant services.

  5. Inform the IT Manager and affected department heads.

  6. Contact the vendor if the issue is application-related.

docs.title: 9.2 Business Continuity
docs.text:
1. Inform the Food & Beverage Manager and affected outlet managers.

  2. Activate the hotel's approved manual billing or contingency process.

  3. Use only authorized manual transaction records.

  4. Maintain clear transaction references and supporting details.

  5. Ensure that financial approvals remain in place.

  6. Avoid duplicate billing when the POS service becomes available again.

docs.title: 9.3 Restoration
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the underlying technical issue has been resolved.

  2. Verify application and terminal availability.

  3. Test order entry and billing.

  4. Verify printer and kitchen order routing.

  5. Test PMS integration where applicable.

  6. Reconcile manual transactions with system records.

  7. Obtain operational confirmation from the outlet manager.

  8. Close the downtime incident after documentation.

docs.title: 10. POS SOFTWARE UPDATE AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT
docs.text: All POS application updates and configuration changes must follow the hotel's approved change management process.

docs.title: 10.1 Software Updates
docs.text:
1. Receive the update notification or vendor recommendation.

  2. Review the purpose, impact, and compatibility of the update.

  3. Coordinate with the vendor and relevant departments.

  4. Obtain approval from the designated authority.

  5. Confirm that the required backup or recovery arrangement is available.

  6. Schedule the update during an approved maintenance window.

  7. Notify affected departments in advance.

  8. Apply the update through the authorized procedure.

  9. Test application login, order entry, billing, printing, and integrations.

  10. Record the update details and test results.

docs.title: 10.2 Configuration Changes
docs.text:
Configuration changes may include:

  • Outlet creation or modification.

  • Printer mapping.

  • Menu category configuration.

  • Tax and service charge configuration.

  • User role changes.

  • Payment configuration.

  • POS-PMS interface settings.

  • Terminal configuration.

Control: Menu prices, tax rules, service charges, payment settings, and other financial configurations must be approved by the authorized business or Finance authority. IT should implement only approved changes.

docs.title: 11. POS BACKUP AND RECOVERY COORDINATION
docs.text: The IT team must ensure that appropriate POS data protection and recovery arrangements are maintained.

docs.title: 11.1 Backup Coordination
docs.text:
1. Identify whether the POS system is cloud-hosted or locally hosted.

  2. Confirm backup responsibilities with the vendor or hosting provider.

  3. Verify that the backup schedule meets hotel requirements.

  4. Review available backup success or failure reports.

  5. Escalate failed or missing backups.

  6. Maintain records of backup status and related incidents.

docs.title: 11.2 Recovery Support
docs.text:
1. Obtain authorization for the recovery activity.

  2. Contact the vendor or authorized system administrator.

  3. Confirm the appropriate recovery point.

  4. Assess the operational and financial impact of restoration.

  5. Perform recovery through the approved technical process.

  6. Validate application availability and transaction integrity.

  7. Coordinate with Finance and F&B for transaction reconciliation.

  8. Document the recovery activity.

docs.title: 12. POS SECURITY MANAGEMENT
docs.text: The POS system may contain commercially sensitive information, transaction records, and guest-related information. Appropriate security controls must be maintained.

docs.title: 12.1 User Security
docs.text:
• Provide individual user accounts.

  • Apply role-based permissions.

  • Restrict administrator access.

  • Disable accounts promptly when access is no longer required.

  • Review privileged access periodically.

  • Do not share passwords or authentication credentials.

docs.title: 12.2 Device Security
docs.text:
• Restrict physical access to POS terminals.

  • Do not allow unauthorized software installation.

  • Apply approved operating system and security updates.

  • Protect POS devices from unauthorized USB or external device usage.

  • Secure unattended terminals.

  • Report lost or stolen devices immediately.

docs.title: 12.3 Network Security
docs.text:
• Place POS devices on an appropriately controlled network.

  • Restrict unnecessary network access.

  • Coordinate firewall and network rule changes through approved processes.

  • Avoid connecting unauthorized devices to POS network segments.

  • Monitor and report suspicious connectivity or access activity.

docs.title: 12.4 Payment Security
docs.text:
Where card payment terminals or payment applications are used:

  • Follow the hotel's payment security policy.

  • Use approved payment service providers and configurations.

  • Do not store card security codes or sensitive authentication data.

  • Restrict access to payment-related configuration.

  • Refer suspected payment security incidents to the designated security and Finance teams.

  • Follow applicable payment security requirements, including PCI DSS where relevant.

docs.title: 13. VENDOR COORDINATION AND SUPPORT
docs.text: The IT Department must maintain an effective support relationship with the POS system vendor.

docs.title: 13.1 Vendor Support Process
docs.text:
1. Identify the issue and affected services.

  2. Perform initial troubleshooting.

  3. Collect relevant error messages, screenshots, logs, and timestamps, ensuring sensitive information is protected.

  4. Create a support ticket with the vendor.

  5. Record the ticket number and assigned support contact.

  6. Monitor progress until resolution.

  7. Test the system after vendor intervention.

  8. Obtain confirmation from the affected department.

  9. Close the incident with proper documentation.

docs.title: 13.2 Vendor Escalation
docs.text:
Escalate issues when:

  • POS services remain unavailable.

  • Financial transactions are affected.

  • PMS integration is interrupted.

  • Repeated application errors occur.

  • Data integrity is suspected.

  • A security incident is identified.

  • Vendor response exceeds the agreed service level.

docs.title: 14. POS INCIDENT DOCUMENTATION
docs.text:
The IT Department must maintain records of POS-related technical activities.

Required records may include:

  1. POS user access register.

  2. POS terminal and device inventory.

  3. Daily POS monitoring checklist.

  4. POS incident and complaint register.

  5. Vendor support ticket register.

  6. Software update and change records.

  7. Backup verification records.

  8. POS-PMS integration incident records.

  9. Downtime and recovery reports.

  10. Preventive maintenance records.

  11. Security incident reports.

  12. Departmental training and handover records, where applicable.

Records must be stored securely and retained according to hotel policy and applicable legal requirements.

docs.title: 15. PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
docs.text:
Frequency Maintenance Activity Responsible Team Daily Check POS application availability IT Daily Verify active POS terminals IT / F&B Daily Check receipt and kitchen printers IT / Outlet Daily Review critical system alerts IT Daily Check POS-PMS integration status IT Weekly Inspect POS terminals and connected devices IT Weekly Review recurring technical incidents IT Weekly Check printer condition and connectivity IT Monthly Review POS user accounts and permissions IT / Department Head Monthly Review vendor tickets and recurring problems IT Monthly Verify backup status and reports IT / Vendor Quarterly Review system access and security controls IT Quarterly Review POS inventory and configuration records IT Annually Review this SOP and support arrangements IT Manager

The schedule may be adjusted according to system architecture, operational requirements, vendor recommendations, and hotel policy.

docs.title: 16. POS INCIDENT ESCALATION MATRIX
docs.text:
Priority Example Issue Initial Response Escalation Critical All POS outlets unavailable Immediate IT Manager, F&B Head, Vendor High POS-PMS integration failure affecting room charges Immediate IT Manager, Front Office, Finance, Vendor High Multiple outlets unable to process orders or bills Immediate IT Manager, F&B Head, Vendor Medium Single POS terminal failure As soon as possible IT Executive / IT Manager Medium Kitchen printer or KDS failure As soon as possible IT / Outlet Manager Low Minor display or reporting issue Within normal support workflow IT Support Low User access or routine configuration request As per approval workflow IT / Department Head

Actual response and resolution targets must follow the hotel's approved IT service levels and vendor agreements.

docs.title: 17. POS PERFORMANCE MONITORING
docs.text:
The IT Manager should periodically review the following indicators:

  • POS application availability.

  • Number of POS-related incidents.

  • Average incident resolution time.

  • Number of recurring terminal failures.

  • Printer and KDS failure frequency.

  • POS-PMS integration failure frequency.

  • Backup success rate, where applicable.

  • Number of unauthorized or inappropriate access incidents.

  • Vendor response and resolution performance.

  • Number of unresolved critical issues.

Performance reports should be reviewed with relevant departments to identify recurring problems and improvement opportunities.

docs.title: 18. DAILY POS OPERATIONS CHECKLIST
docs.text:
IT Department Daily Checklist

  • Confirm POS application availability.

  • Verify active POS terminals.

  • Check terminal network connectivity.

  • Verify receipt printer functionality.

  • Verify kitchen printer and KDS functionality.

  • Check POS-PMS integration status, where applicable.

  • Review critical error messages and alerts.

  • Check reported POS complaints.

  • Review unresolved vendor tickets.

  • Update the POS incident register.

  • Confirm that critical issues have been escalated.

Food & Beverage Department Checklist

  • Confirm that authorized staff can log in.

  • Verify order entry functionality.

  • Confirm that orders reach the correct kitchen printer or display.

  • Verify billing functionality.

  • Report any transaction or integration issue to IT.

  • Follow the approved downtime procedure when required.

docs.title: 19. HOTEL-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
docs.text:
This SOP is designed as a general framework and should be adapted to the hotel's POS environment.

Examples of POS platforms used in the hospitality industry include:

  • Oracle MICROS Simphony.

  • Infor POS solutions.

  • IDS Next POS.

  • eZee POS.

  • Other cloud-based and locally hosted hospitality POS applications.

The exact procedures may vary depending on the system and its configuration.

Before implementation, the hotel should document:

  1. POS application name and version.

  2. Vendor and support contact details.

  3. Number and location of POS terminals.

  4. Restaurant, bar, banquet, and other outlet configurations.

  5. POS server or cloud hosting details.

  6. POS-PMS integration architecture.

  7. Payment terminal integration details.

  8. Backup and recovery responsibilities.

  9. Approved downtime and manual billing procedures.

  10. Departmental approval responsibilities.

Important: System-specific instructions should be maintained as implementation notes or supporting documents. The core SOP should remain consistent across the hotel's POS operations.

docs.title: 20. COMPLIANCE AND EXCEPTIONS
docs.text:
All departments using the POS system must follow the approved procedures described in this SOP.

Any exception must be:

  • Documented with a clear reason.

  • Reviewed by the relevant department head.

  • Approved by the authorized management representative.

  • Recorded by IT where technical access or configuration is affected.

Any suspected unauthorized access, transaction manipulation, data loss, or payment security incident must be reported through the hotel's established incident reporting process.

docs.title: 21. SOP REVIEW AND REVISION HISTORY
docs.text:
This SOP must be reviewed at least annually or whenever a major change occurs in the POS application, infrastructure, integration, security requirements, or hotel operating procedures.
